Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 34, verses 1–2:

Tafsir of Surat Saba'

It is a Meccan surah.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

He, may He be exalted, informs about His noble Self: that to Him belongs absolute praise in this world and in the Hereafter, because He is the Bestower of blessings and favours upon the people of this world and the Hereafter, the Owner of all of that, and the Judge in all of that, as He said: ﴿And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs praise in the first and the last, and to Him is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 70]. For this reason He said here: ﴿Praise be to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.﴾ That is, all of it is His possession, His servants, and under His dominion and control, as He said: ﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life].﴾ [Al-Layl: 13].

Then He said: ﴿And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter﴾. So He is the One worshipped forever, the One praised throughout all time. And He said: ﴿And He is the Wise﴾, that is, in His statements, His actions, His legislation and His decree, ﴿the All-Aware﴾, the One from whom no hidden thing is concealed, and nothing is absent from Him.

Malik related from al-Zuhri: "Aware of His creation, Wise in His command." For this reason He said: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it﴾, that is, He knows the number of the drops of rain that descend into the parts of the earth, and the seeds that are sown and that lie hidden in it, and He knows what emerges from that: its number, its form and its attributes. ﴿And what descends from the sky﴾, that is, of rain and provision. ﴿And what ascends into it﴾, that is, of righteous deeds and other things. ﴿And He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving﴾, that is, the Most Merciful to His servants, so He does not hasten to punish their disobedient ones, the Oft-Forgiving of the sins of His servants who turn back to Him in repentance and put their trust in Him.

Malik related from al-Zuhri: "Aware of His creation, Wise in His command." This is one of the three verses that have no fourth like them, in which Allah commanded His Messenger ﷺ to swear by his Lord, the Mighty, concerning the occurrence of the Return (al-ma'ad), when it was denied by those among the people of disbelief and obstinacy who denied it. The first of them is in Surah Yunus: ﴿And they ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you cannot escape it."﴾ [Yunus: 53]. The second is this one: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you."﴾. The third is in Surah at-Taghabun: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah."﴾ [at-Taghabun: 7]. So His saying: ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you"﴾ [[In T: "ليأتينكم" (liya'tiyannakum).]], then He described Himself with what confirms and establishes that: ﴿the Knower of the unseen, from whom not an atom's weight is hidden in the heavens or on the earth, nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register﴾.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿Is not hidden from Him﴾ means: is not absent from Him, i.e., everything is included within His knowledge, so nothing of it is concealed from Him. Thus, even if the bones decay, scatter and are torn apart, He knows wherever they go and wherever they are dispersed. Then He will restore them as He originated them the first time, for He is Knowing of everything.

Then He explained His wisdom in restoring the bodies and establishing the Hour by His saying: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds. Those will have forgiveness and a noble provision. But those who strove against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them, for them is a painful punishment of an evil nature.﴾ That is: those who strove to hinder from the way of Allah and to deny His messengers. ﴿For them is a painful punishment of an evil nature﴾. That is: so that He may bless the happy among the believers and punish the wretched among the disbelievers, as He said: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the triumphant﴾ [al-Hashr: 20], and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Shall We treat those who believed and did righteous deeds like those who cause corruption on the earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28].

His saying: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾. This is another wisdom, joined to the one before it. It means that the believers in what was sent down to the messengers, when they witness the establishment of the Hour and the recompense of the righteous and the wicked according to what they had been taught of Allah's books in the world, will then see it with the certainty of sight (ʿayn al-yaqin). On that Day they will also say: ﴿The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth﴾ [al-A'raf: 43]. It will also be said: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke truly﴾ [Ya-Sin: 52], and ﴿You had remained, by the decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection﴾ [ar-Rum: 56]. And ﴿those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. Al-'Aziz is the one of impregnable dominion (al-Mani' al-Janab), who cannot be overcome nor resisted, but has subdued everything. Al-Hamid is praiseworthy in all His sayings, actions, legislation and decree, and He is the One praised in all of that.

And the earth — We spread it out, and how excellent are We as the spreaders﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 47–48].

Abd ibn Humayd said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Have they not considered what is before them and what is behind them of the sky and the earth?﴾, he said: Indeed, if you look to your right or to your left, or in front of you or behind you, you will see the sky and the earth.

Sufyan said, from Qatadah: "al-Muneeb" is one who turns toward Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 34, verses 12–13:**

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned what He bestowed upon Dawud, He followed it with mention of what He gave his son Sulayman [^1], namely the subjugation of the wind for him, carrying his carpet: its morning journey was a month and its evening journey was a month.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: He would set out in the morning on his carpet from Damascus and land at Istakhr, where he would have his midday meal. Then he would depart in the evening from Istakhr and spend the night at Kabul. The distance between Damascus and Istakhr is a full month's journey for a swift traveler, and the distance between Istakhr and Kabul is also a full month's journey for a swift traveler.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata al-Khurasani, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others than one, said: al-Qitr is copper. Qatadah said: It was in Yemen, and everything that people fashion from it is from what Allah, the Exalted, brought forth for Sulayman, peace be upon him.

Al-Suddi said: It was made to flow for him for only three days.

* *

His saying: ﴿And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord﴾. That is, We subjected the jinn to him, so they worked before him by the permission of Allah, that is, by His decree [^2], and by His subjugating them to him by His will, to build whatever he wished of structures and other things. ﴿And whoever of them deviates from Our command﴾, that is, whoever turns aside and departs from obedience among them, ﴿We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze﴾, which is the burning fire.

Ibn Abi Hatim has related here a strange hadith. He said: My father related to us, Abu Salih related to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to us, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The jinn are of three kinds: a kind that has wings and flies in the air, a kind that are snakes and dogs, and a kind that settle and move about." Its raising to the Prophet ﷺ is extremely strange [^3].

He also said: My father related to us, Harmalah related to us, Ibn Wahb related to us, Bakr ibn Mudar informed me, from Muhammad, from Ibn An'um, that he said: The jinn are three: a kind for whom there is reward and upon whom there is punishment, a kind that fly between heaven and earth, and a kind that are snakes and dogs.

Bakr ibn Mudar said: I do not know except that he said: He related to me that mankind are three: a kind whom Allah shades with the shadow of His Throne on the Day of Resurrection; a kind who are like cattle, nay, they are even more astray in the way; and a kind who appear in the forms of people with the hearts of devils.

He also said: My father related to us: 'Ali ibn Hashim ibn Marzuq related to us, Salamah, that is Ibn al-Fadl, related to us, from Isma'il, from al-Hasan, who said: The jinn are the offspring of Iblis, and mankind are the offspring of Adam. Among both groups there are believers, and among both groups there are unbelievers. They are partners with them in reward and punishment. Whoever among both groups is a believer is a friend of Allah, and whoever among both groups is a disbeliever is a devil.

* *

His saying: ﴿They made for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries and statues﴾. As for al-Mahareeb (sanctuaries), they are fine构造 buildings, and it is the most noble thing in the dwelling and its front part.

Mujahid said: al-Mahareeb are buildings below the palaces. al-Dahhak said: They are the mosques. Qatadah said: They are the mosques and the palaces. Ibn Zayd said: They are the dwellings. As for al-Tamathil (statues), 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: al-Tamathil are the images. Mujahid said: They were made of copper. Qatadah said: They were of clay and glass.

* *

His saying: ﴿And bowls like cisterns, and fixed cooking pots﴾. Al-Jawab is the plural of jabiyah, which is the basin in which water is collected, as al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays said:

*It is brought around to the family of al-Mahalliq, a bowl*
*like the basin of the Iraqi shaykh, overflowing.* [^4]

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿like al-Jawab﴾, that is, like a hollow in the ground.

al-'Awfi related from him: like reservoirs. Likewise said Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and others.

And al-Qudur al-Rasiyat (the fixed cooking pots): that is, the firmly established ones, in their places, that do not move or shift from their places because of their great size. Thus said Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others.

'Ikrimah said: Their supports are part of them.

* *

His saying: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾. That is, We said to them: Work in gratitude for what He has bestowed upon you in this world and in religion.

*Shukran* (in gratitude) is a verbal noun from a verb not of the same root, or it is an object of purpose. On both analyses, there is an indication that gratitude occurs through action, as it occurs through speech and through intention, as the poet said:

*Blessings from me have benefited you in three ways: my hand, my tongue, and the hidden heart.*

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli said: Prayer is gratitude, fasting is gratitude, and every good deed you do for Allah is gratitude, and the best gratitude is praise. Ibn Jarir related it.

He and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: Gratitude is fear of Allah and righteous deeds.

This is said of one who is engaged in the action, and the family of Dawud, peace be upon him, were indeed like that, standing in gratitude to Allah in word and deed.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to us, Ja'far, that is Ibn Sulayman, related to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, who said: Dawud, peace be upon him, had divided the prayer among his family, his children and his wives, so that there was never an hour of the night or day in which one of the family of Dawud was not standing in prayer. This verse overwhelmed them: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude, but few of My servants are grateful﴾.

In the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of Dawud: he would sleep half the night, stand for a third of it, and sleep for a sixth of it. And the most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of Dawud: he would fast one day and break his fast the next day, and he would not flee when he met the enemy." [^5]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Majah related, from the hadith of Sunayd ibn Dawud, who said: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir related to us, from his father, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The mother of Sulayman ibn Dawud said to Sulayman: O my son, do not sleep much at night, for much sleep at night leaves a man poor on the Day of Resurrection." [^6]

Ibn Abi Hatim related here, from Dawud, peace be upon him, a very lengthy and strange report. He also said:

My father related to us, 'Imran ibn Musa related to us, Abu Yazid, Fayd ibn Ishaq al-Raqqi related to us, who said: Fudayl said concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾: Dawud said: O Lord, how can I thank You, when gratitude itself is a blessing from You? He said: "Now you have thanked Me, since you have come to know that the blessing is from Me."

* *

His saying: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾: it is a report of what actually happens.

In the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of Dawud: he would sleep half the night, stand for a third of it, and sleep for a sixth of it. And the most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of Dawud: he would fast one day and break his fast the next day, and he would not flee when he met the enemy." [^5]

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Majah related, from the hadith of Sunayd ibn Dawud, who said: Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir related to us, from his father, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The mother of Sulayman ibn Dawud said to Sulayman: O my son, do not sleep much at night, for much sleep at night leaves a man poor on the Day of Resurrection." [^6]

Ibn Abi Hatim related here, from Dawud, peace be upon him, a very lengthy and strange report. He also said:

My father related to us, 'Imran ibn Musa related to us, Abu Yazid, Fayd ibn Ishaq al-Raqqi related to us, who said: Fudayl said concerning the words of the Exalted: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾: Dawud said: O Lord, how can I thank You, when gratitude itself is a blessing from You? He said: "Now you have thanked Me, since you have come to know that the blessing is from Me."

* *

His saying: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾: it is a report of what actually happens.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 34, verse 14:

He, may He be exalted, mentions the manner of the death of Sulayman (peace be upon him), and how Allah concealed his death from the jinn who were subjected to him in arduous labours. For he remained leaning on his staff, which was his mansa'ah (staff), as Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others besides them said, for a long period, approximately a year. When the earth-creature, which is the termite (al-aradah), consumed it, it weakened and fell to the ground, and it became known that he had died a long time before that. The jinn and mankind then also clearly saw that the jinn do not know the unseen, as they had been imagining and making people believe.

There is a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith concerning this, which is gharib (strange), and its authenticity is open to question. Ibn Jarir said:

Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated to us: Musa ibn Mas'ud Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to us, from 'Ata', from al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Sulayman, the Prophet of Allah, peace be upon him, when he prayed, would see a tree growing before him, and he would say to it: 'What is your name?' It would say: 'So-and-so.' He would say: 'For what purpose are you?' If it was for planting, it was planted; and if it was for medicine, it was written down. One day, while he was praying, he saw a tree before him, and he said to it: 'What is your name?' It said: 'Al-kharrub (carob).' He said: 'For what purpose are you?' It said: 'For the ruin of this house.' Sulayman said: 'O Allah, conceal my death from the jinn, until mankind knows that the jinn do not know the unseen.' He then carved it into a staff, and he leaned upon it for a year dead, while the jinn were working. Then the termite consumed it, and mankind realised that if the jinn had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating torment."

He said: Ibn 'Abbas used to recite it thus, and he said: "So the jinn thanked the termite, and it used to bring it water."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it in this way, from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, with the same chain. In its being traced to the Prophet there is strangeness and irregularity, and the more likely position is that it is mawquf (stopping at a companion). 'Ata' ibn Abi Muslim al-Khurasani has strange reports, and in some of his hadith there is irregularity.

al-Suddi said, in a hadith he related from Abu Malik, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murrah al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some people among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Sulayman would retreat into Bayt al-Maqdis for a year, two years, a month, two months, and less or more than that, and his food and drink would be brought in to him. He was brought in on the occasion in which he died. The beginning of that was that there was not a day on which he woke up except that a tree grew in Bayt al-Maqdis. He would come to it and ask it: "What is your name?" It would say: "My name is so-and-so." If it was for planting, he would plant it; and if it was a medicinal plant, it would say: "I am a medicinal plant for such-and-such." He would keep it so, until a tree grew which was called al-kharrubah, and he asked it: "What is your name?" It said: "I am al-kharrubah." He said: "And for what purpose did you grow?" It said: "I grew for the ruin of this mosque." Sulayman said: "Would Allah ruin it while I am alive? You are the one whose purpose is my destruction and the ruin of Bayt al-Maqdis." He uprooted it and planted it in one of his gardens, then entered the sanctuary (mihrab), stood praying, leaning on his staff, and he died, and the devils did not know of him, while they were working for him, fearing that he would come out and punish them. The devils used to gather around the mihrab, and the mihrab had openings before him and behind him. The devil who wished to escape would say: "Are you not strong enough, if I enter and come out from that side?" So he would enter until he came out from the other side. One of those devils entered and passed through, and no devil looked at Sulayman in the mihrab without being burned. He passed and did not hear Sulayman's voice; then he returned and did not hear; then he returned and fell into the house and was not burned. He looked at Sulayman, peace be upon him, and saw that he had fallen dead. He went out and informed the people that Sulayman had died. They opened up the place around him and brought him out. They found his mansa'ah, which is the staff in the language of Abyssinia, eaten by the termite, and they did not know since how long he had died. So they placed the termite upon the staff, and it ate from it for a day and a night. Then they calculated on that basis, and found that he had died a year earlier. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "They remained toiling for him after his death for a full year." So at that point the people became certain that the jinn had been lying to them, for if they had known the unseen, they would have known of Sulayman's death, and would not have remained in the torment, labouring for him for a year. This is the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Then when We decreed death upon him, nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. So when he fell, the jinn saw clearly that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating torment﴾. He says: their affair became clear to the people, that they had been lying to them. Then the devils said to the termite: "If you ate food, we would bring you the finest food, and if you drank drink, we would give you the finest drink; but we will transport to you water and clay," and they used to carry that to it wherever it was. He said: "Have you not seen the clay that is found inside wood? That is what the devils bring to it, out of gratitude to it."

This report, and Allah knows best, is only among what was taken from the scholars of the People of the Book, and it is a statement of a companion. What of it is not to be accepted except what agrees with the truth, and not to be rejected except what contradicts the truth, and what remains is neither to be affirmed nor denied.

Ibn Wahb and Asbagh ibn al-Faraj said, on the authority of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning His saying: ﴿nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff﴾: He said: Sulayman, peace be upon him, said to the Angel of Death: "When you are commanded concerning me, inform me." So he came to him and said: "O Sulayman, I have been commanded concerning you; a little moment remains for you." So he summoned the devils, and they built around him a palace of glass, with no door. He stood praying and leaned on his staff. He said: The Angel of Death entered upon him and seized his soul while he was leaning on his staff, and he did not do that to flee from the Angel of Death. He said: The jinn were working before him and looking at him, thinking that he was alive. He said: Then Allah, mighty and majestic, sent the earth-creature. He said: The creature eats wood, and it is called al-qadih; it entered into it and ate it, until when it had eaten the inside of the staff, it became weak and it became heavy upon it, and it fell dead. When the jinn saw that, they dispersed and departed. He said: That is His saying: ﴿nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff﴾. Asbagh said: It has reached me from another that it remained for a year eating from it before it fell.

Several of the early scholars have mentioned something similar to this, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 34, verses 15–17 (part 1 of 2):

Saba' were the kings of Yemen and its people. Among them were the Tubba'ah (the Tubba' kings), and Bilqis, the companion of Sulayman (peace be upon him), was among them. They lived in blessing and prosperity in their land, in their livelihood, in the abundance of their provisions, their crops and their fruits. Allah sent Messengers to them, commanding them to eat of His provision and to thank Him by affirming His oneness (tawhid) and worshipping Him. They remained so for as long as Allah willed, then they turned away from what they had been commanded. So they were punished by the sending of the flood and by being scattered throughout the lands, "the hands of Saba', scattered completely" (shadhara madhar), as its detail and explanation will come shortly, if Allah the Exalted wills, and in Him is trust.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Hubayrah, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa'lah, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about Saba': "What is it? Is it a man, a woman or a land?" He said: "Rather, it is a man who had ten sons. Six of them settled in Yemen and four in al-Sham. As for the Yemenis: they are Madhhij, Kindah, al-Azd, al-Ash'ariyyun, Anmar, and Himyar. As for the Shamiyyah: they are Lakhm, Judham, 'Amilah and Ghassan."

'Abd (ibn Humayd) also narrated it from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'ah, with it (Musnad 1/316). This chain is hasan (sound), and they did not record it. [It has been narrated through multiple paths.] It was also narrated by the Hafiz Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr in his book "al-Qasd wal-Umam bi-Ma'rifat Usul Ansab al-'Arab wal-'Ajam", from the hadith of Ibn Lahi'ah, from 'Alqamah ibn Wa'lah, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned something similar. Something similar has also been narrated by another route.

Imam Ahmad also said, together with 'Abd ibn Humayd: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Abu Janab Yahya ibn Abi Hayyah al-Kalbi narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hani ibn 'Urwah, from Farwah ibn Musayk, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I fight those who turn back from my people, from among those who face forward?" He said: "Yes, fight those who turn back from your people with those who face forward." When I turned away, he called me and said: "Do not fight them until you invite them to Islam." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about Saba'? Is it a valley, or a man, or what is it?" He said: "No, rather it is a man from the Arabs, who had ten sons. Six of them went to the right (tayammana) and four went to the left (tasha'ama). Those who went to the right were al-Azd, al-Ash'ariyyun, Himyar, Kindah, Madhhij, and Anmar, who are called Bajilah and Khath'am. Lakhm, Judham, 'Amilah and Ghassan went to the left."

This too is a jayyid (good) chain, although Abu Janab al-Kalbi is in it, and they have spoken about him (Ibn Hajar mentioned it in Atraf al-Musnad 5/178, and it is not in the printed Musnad). However, Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from al-'Anqazi, from Asbat ibn Nasr, from Yahya ibn Hani al-Muradi, from his paternal uncle or his father, Asbat being in doubt, who said: Farwah ibn Musayk came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned it (Tafsir al-Tabari 22/53).

Another route for this hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, from Tawbah ibn Namir, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya, that he told him, who said: We were with 'Ubaydah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman in Ifriqiyah, and he said one day: "I do not think there is a people in any land except that they are its people." 'Ali ibn Rabah said: "No, so-and-so narrated to me that Farwah ibn Musayk al-Ghutayfi came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Saba' is a people who had might in the Jahiliyyah, and I fear they will apostatize from Islam; shall I fight them?' He said: 'I have not been commanded anything concerning them yet.'" Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, there was for Saba' in their dwelling a sign﴾ until the end of the verses. A man said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, what is Saba'?" and he mentioned a hadith similar to the previous one: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about Saba': "What is it? Is it a land, a man, or a woman?" He said: "Rather, it is a man who had ten sons; six of them settled in Yemen and four in al-Sham. As for the Yemenis: they are Madhhij, Kindah, al-Azd, al-Ash'ariyyun, Anmar, and Himyar, other than those who settled there. As for al-Sham: they are Lakhm, Judham, Ghassan, and 'Amilah."

In it there is an oddity regarding the mention of the revelation of the verse in Madinah, whereas the surah is entirely Makkan, and Allah knows best.

Another route: Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Hakam narrated to me, Abu Sabrah al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from Farwah ibn Musayk al-Ghutayfi, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, inform me about Saba': what is it? Is it a land or a woman?" He said: "It is neither a land nor a woman, but it is a man to whom ten children were born. Six of them went to the right and four went to the left. As for those who went to the left: they are Lakhm, Judham, 'Amilah and Ghassan. As for those who went to the right: they are Kindah, al-Ash'ariyyun, al-Azd, Madhhij, Himyar and Anmar." A man said: "What is Anmar?" He said: "Those from whom are Khath'am and Bajilah."

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in his Jami', from Abu Kurayb and 'Abd ibn Humayd, both of whom said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, and he mentioned it in a more expanded form. Then he said: "This is a hadith hasan gharib" (Tafsir al-Tabari 22/53 and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3222).

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sufyan narrated to us, Qasim ibn Asbagh narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Najdah al-Hawti narrated to us, Ibn Kathir narrated to us—he is 'Uthman ibn Kathir—from al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Musa ibn 'Ali, from Yazid ibn Husayn, from Tamim al-Dari, that a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him about Saba', and he mentioned something similar. Thus this hadith was strengthened and graded hasan (al-Qasd wal-Umam p. 20).

The genealogists, among them Muhammad ibn Ishaq, said: the name of Saba' is 'Abd Shams ibn Yashjub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan.

He was named Saba' because he was the first among the Arabs to take captives (saba'a). He was also called al-Ra'ish, because he was the first to take booty in battle and give it to his people; thus he was called al-Ra'ish, and the Arabs call wealth rish and riyash. They also mention that he gave glad tidings of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his earlier time, and he said in that regard a poem:

"After us he will possess a great kingdom,
a prophet who does not permit what is forbidden...
And after him kings from among them will rule,
who will subject the servants without blame...
And after them kings from among us will rule,
and sovereignty among us will become by division...
And after Qahtan a prophet will rule,
pious, Khabtah, the best of mankind...
And he will be named Ahmad, would that I
were to live a year after his mission...
So I will support him and grant him my help,
with every armored man and every archer...
When he appears, be his helpers,
and whoever meets him, convey my greetings to him."

Al-Hamdani mentioned this in his book "al-Iklil".

They differed concerning Qahtan on three views:

The first: that he is of the lineage of Iram ibn Sam ibn Nuh, and they differed on how his lineage connects to him in three ways.

The second: that he is of the lineage of 'Abir, who is Hud, peace be upon him, and they differed on how his lineage connects to him in three ways as well.

The third: that he is of the lineage of Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Khalil, peace be upon them both, and they differed on how his lineage connects to him in three ways as well. This has been discussed thoroughly by the Hafiz Imam Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr al-Namari, may Allah have mercy on him, in his book entitled "al-Inbah 'ala Dhikr Usul al-Qaba'il al-Ruwat."

The meaning of his saying, peace be upon him, "he was a man from the Arabs," refers to the 'Arab al-'Ariba, who existed before al-Khalil, peace be upon him, from the lineage of Sam ibn Nuh. According to the third view, he was from the lineage of al-Khalil, peace be upon him, but this is not well known among them, and Allah knows best. However, in Sahih al-Bukhari: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a group of men from Aslam who were shooting arrows, and he said: "Shoot, O sons of Isma'il, for your father was an archer" (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3507, from the hadith of Salamah, may Allah be pleased with him). Aslam is a tribe of the Ansar, and the Ansar, both the Aws and the Khazraj, are from Ghassan, from the Arabs of Yemen, from Saba'. They settled in Yathrib when Saba' were scattered throughout the lands, when Allah sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim, and a group of them settled in al-Sham. They were called Ghassan after a water (ma') where they settled; it was said: in Yemen. It was also said: it is near al-Mushallal, as Hassan ibn Thabit said:

"If you ask, we are a noble group,
al-Azd is our lineage, and al-Ma' is Ghassan."

The meaning of his saying "He had ten sons from the Arabs" is: from his offspring were these ten who are the origins of the tribes of Yemen's Arabs, not that they were born from his loins directly; rather, between him and some of them there are two or three fathers, or fewer or more, as is established and clarified in its places in the books of genealogy.

The meaning of his saying "So six of them went to the right, and four of them went to the left" is: after Allah sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim, some of them remained in their lands, and some departed from them to other places. Concerning the dam: the water used to come to them from between two mountains, and the floodwaters of their rains and valleys also gathered there. Their ancient kings therefore purposed to build between them a great, firm dam, until the water rose and was held back on the slopes of those two mountains. They planted trees and harvested fruits in the greatest abundance and beauty, as more than one of the salaf mentioned, among them Qatadah: that a woman would walk under the trees with a basket or a container on her head, in which fruit was gathered, and what would fall from the trees would fill it without any need for effort or picking, because of its abundance, ripeness and evenness. This dam was at Ma'rib, a town three stages from Sana'a, and it is known as the Dam of Ma'rib.

Others mentioned that there was in their land no fly, no mosquito, no flea, and no vermin of any kind, due to the moderation of the air, the soundness of their temperament, and Allah's care for them, so that they would believe in His oneness and worship Him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, there was for Saba' in their dwelling a sign﴾. Then He explained it with His saying: ﴿Two gardens on the right and on the left﴾, that is, from the two sides of the two mountains, with the town between them. ﴿Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him: a good land and a Lord Forgiving﴾, that is, Forgiving of you if you persist in monotheism.

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 34, verse 15–17 (part 2 of 2):

His saying: ﴿But they turned away﴾, meaning: from the Oneness of Allah, from worshipping Him, and from giving thanks for what He had bestowed upon them; and they turned to the worship of the sun, as the hoopoe of Solomon said: ﴿And I have come to you from Saba' with certain news. Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne. I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appealing to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided﴾ [An-Naml: 22, 24].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: Allah sent to them thirteen prophets.

As-Suddi said: Allah sent to them twelve thousand prophets, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim﴾. It has been said: al-'Arim means the waters. It has been said: the valley. It has been said: the rat. It has been said: the abundant water. It is then of the type of the attribution of a noun to its qualifier, like "the mosque of the congregation" (masjid al-jami'). And "Sa'id Kurz" — Al-Suhayli (d. 581 AH) related this (Ar-Rawd al-Unf, 1/15).

Among those who mentioned this were a number of scholars, including Ibn 'Abbas, Wahb ibn Munabbih, Qatadah, and ad-Dahhak, that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed to punish them by sending al-'Arim upon them, He sent upon the dam a creature from the earth, called "al-Juradh" (the rat), which gnawed through it. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They used to find in their books that the cause of the ruin of this dam was the rat, so for a period of time they would keep cats at it. But when the decree came, the mice overcame the cats, entered the dam, gnawed through it, and it collapsed upon them.

Qatadah and others said: al-Juradh is al-Khuld (the mole), which gnawed at its foundations until it became weak and crumbled. When the days of torrents came, the water struck the structure and it fell. The water flowed down to the bottom of the valley and destroyed what lay before it of buildings, trees, and other things. The water receded from the trees that were on the two mountains to the right and left, so they dried up and were shattered, and those fruitful, lush, green trees were replaced, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and as-Suddi said: It is al-Arak (the toothbrush tree) and the fruit of the lote-tree (akl al-bariir).

﴿And tamarisk﴾: al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas that it is al-tarfa' (tamarisk).

Others said: it is a tree resembling the tamarisk. It has also been said: it is the acacia (samur). And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a few lote-trees﴾: Since the best of these trees that were exchanged was the lote-tree, He said: ﴿And a few lote-trees﴾. Thus, the state to which those two gardens were brought—after the ripe fruits, the pleasant sights, the deep shades, and the flowing rivers—was changed into the arak tree, the tamarisk, and the lote-tree with many thorns and little fruit. This was because of their disbelief and polytheism toward Allah, their denial of the truth, and their turning away from it to falsehood. Therefore He said: ﴿That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. And do We recompense except the ungrateful?﴾, meaning: We punished them for their disbelief.

Mujahid said: "And none is punished except the ungrateful."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Allah the Mighty has spoken truly. None is punished for the like of their deed except the ungrateful." Tawus said: "None is called to account except the ungrateful."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Abu 'Umar ibn an-Nahhas ar-Ramli related to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad related to us, Abu al-Bayda' related to us, from Hisham ibn Salih at-Taghlibi, from Ibn Khirah—and he was among the companions of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him—who said: "The recompense for disobedience is weakness in worship, narrowness in livelihood, and difficulty in pleasure." It was said: "And what is difficulty in pleasure?" He said: "No lawful pleasure is met except that someone comes to spoil it for him."

Saba' were the kings of Yemen and its people. Among them were the Tubba'ah (the Tubba' kings), and Bilqis, the companion of Sulayman (peace be upon him), was among them. They lived in blessing and prosperity in their land, in their livelihood, in the abundance of their provisions, their crops and their fruits. Is it a man, a woman or a land?" He said: "Rather, it is a man who had ten sons. Six of them settled in Yemen and four in al-Sham. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about Saba'? Is it a valley, or a man, or what is it?" He said: "No, rather it is a man from the Arabs, who had ten sons. As for those who went to the left: they are Lakhm, Judham, 'Amilah and Ghassan. As for those who went to the right: they are Kindah, al-Ash'ariyyun, al-Azd, Madhhij, Himyar and Anmar." "After us he will possess a great kingdom,

And after him kings from among them will rule,
who will subject the servants without blame...

and sovereignty among us will become by division...

They were called Ghassan after a water (ma') where they settled; it was said: in Yemen. It was also said: it is near al-Mushallal, as Hassan ibn Thabit said:

"If you ask, we are a noble group,
al-Azd is our lineage, and al-Ma' is Ghassan."

Concerning the dam: the water used to come to them from between two mountains, and the floodwaters of their rains and valleys also gathered there. Their ancient kings therefore purposed to build between them a great, firm dam, until the water rose and was held back on the slopes of those two mountains. They planted trees and harvested fruits in the greatest abundance and beauty, as more than one of the salaf mentioned, among them Qatadah: that a woman would walk under the trees with a basket or a container on her head, in which fruit was gathered, and what would fall from the trees would fill it without any need for effort or picking, because of its abundance, ripeness and evenness. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 34, verse 15–17 (part 2 of 2):

His saying: ﴿But they turned away﴾, meaning: from the Oneness of Allah, from worshipping Him, and from giving thanks for what He had bestowed upon them; and they turned to the worship of the sun, as the hoopoe of Solomon said: ﴿And I have come to you from Saba' with certain news. Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne. I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of Allah, and Satan has made their deeds appealing to them and averted them from the way, so they are not guided﴾ [An-Naml: 22, 24].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: Allah sent to them thirteen prophets.

As-Suddi said: Allah sent to them twelve thousand prophets, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim﴾. It has been said: al-'Arim means the waters. It has been said: the valley. It has been said: the rat. It has been said: the abundant water. It is then of the type of the attribution of a noun to its qualifier, like "the mosque of the congregation" (masjid al-jami'). And "Sa'id Kurz" — Al-Suhayli (d. 581 AH) related this (Ar-Rawd al-Unf, 1/15).

Among those who mentioned this were a number of scholars, including Ibn 'Abbas, Wahb ibn Munabbih, Qatadah, and ad-Dahhak, that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed to punish them by sending al-'Arim upon them, He sent upon the dam a creature from the earth, called "al-Juradh" (the rat), which gnawed through it. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They used to find in their books that the cause of the ruin of this dam was the rat, so for a period of time they would keep cats at it. But when the decree came, the mice overcame the cats, entered the dam, gnawed through it, and it collapsed upon them.

Qatadah and others said: al-Juradh is al-Khuld (the mole), which gnawed at its foundations until it became weak and crumbled. When the days of torrents came, the water struck the structure and it fell. The water flowed down to the bottom of the valley and destroyed what lay before it of buildings, trees, and other things. The water receded from the trees that were on the two mountains to the right and left, so they dried up and were shattered, and those fruitful, lush, green trees were replaced, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and as-Suddi said: It is al-Arak (the toothbrush tree) and the fruit of the lote-tree (akl al-bariir).

﴿And tamarisk﴾: al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas that it is al-tarfa' (tamarisk).

Others said: it is a tree resembling the tamarisk. It has also been said: it is the acacia (samur). And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a few lote-trees﴾: Since the best of these trees that were exchanged was the lote-tree, He said: ﴿And a few lote-trees﴾. Thus, the state to which those two gardens were brought—after the ripe fruits, the pleasant sights, the deep shades, and the flowing rivers—was changed into the arak tree, the tamarisk, and the lote-tree with many thorns and little fruit. This was because of their disbelief and polytheism toward Allah, their denial of the truth, and their turning away from it to falsehood. Therefore He said: ﴿That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. And do We recompense except the ungrateful?﴾, meaning: We punished them for their disbelief.

Mujahid said: "And none is punished except the ungrateful."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Allah the Mighty has spoken truly. None is punished for the like of their deed except the ungrateful." Tawus said: "None is called to account except the ungrateful."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Abu 'Umar ibn an-Nahhas ar-Ramli related to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad related to us, Abu al-Bayda' related to us, from Hisham ibn Salih at-Taghlibi, from Ibn Khirah—and he was among the companions of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him—who said: "The recompense for disobedience is weakness in worship, narrowness in livelihood, and difficulty in pleasure." It was said: "And what is difficulty in pleasure?" He said: "No lawful pleasure is met except that someone comes to spoil it for him."

Indeed, I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Wahb ibn Munabbih: Allah sent to them thirteen prophets.

As-Suddi said: Allah sent to them twelve thousand prophets, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim﴾. It has been said: al-'Arim means the waters. It has been said: the valley. It has been said: the rat. It has been said: the abundant water. It is then of the type of the attribution of a noun to its qualifier, like "the mosque of the congregation" (masjid al-jami'). And "Sa'id Kurz" — Al-Suhayli (d. 581 AH) related this (Ar-Rawd al-Unf, 1/15).

Among those who mentioned this were a number of scholars, including Ibn 'Abbas, Wahb ibn Munabbih, Qatadah, and ad-Dahhak, that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed to punish them by sending al-'Arim upon them, He sent upon the dam a creature from the earth, called "al-Juradh" (the rat), which gnawed through it. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They used to find in their books that the cause of the ruin of this dam was the rat, so for a period of time they would keep cats at it. But when the decree came, the mice overcame the cats, entered the dam, gnawed through it, and it collapsed upon them.

Qatadah and others said: al-Juradh is al-Khuld (the mole), which gnawed at its foundations until it became weak and crumbled. When the days of torrents came, the water struck the structure and it fell. The water flowed down to the bottom of the valley and destroyed what lay before it of buildings, trees, and other things. The water receded from the trees that were on the two mountains to the right and left, so they dried up and were shattered, and those fruitful, lush, green trees were replaced, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and as-Suddi said: It is al-Arak (the toothbrush tree) and the fruit of the lote-tree (akl al-bariir).

﴿And tamarisk﴾: al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas that it is al-tarfa' (tamarisk).

Others said: it is a tree resembling the tamarisk. It has also been said: it is the acacia (samur). And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And a few lote-trees﴾: Since the best of these trees that were exchanged was the lote-tree, He said: ﴿And a few lote-trees﴾. Thus, the state to which those two gardens were brought—after the ripe fruits, the pleasant sights, the deep shades, and the flowing rivers—was changed into the arak tree, the tamarisk, and the lote-tree with many thorns and little fruit. This was because of their disbelief and polytheism toward Allah, their denial of the truth, and their turning away from it to falsehood. Therefore He said: ﴿That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. And do We recompense except the ungrateful?﴾, meaning: We punished them for their disbelief.

Mujahid said: "And none is punished except the ungrateful."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Allah the Mighty has spoken truly. None is punished for the like of their deed except the ungrateful." Tawus said: "None is called to account except the ungrateful."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Abu 'Umar ibn an-Nahhas ar-Ramli related to us, Hajjaj ibn Muhammad related to us, Abu al-Bayda' related to us, from Hisham ibn Salih at-Taghlibi, from Ibn Khirah—and he was among the companions of 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him—who said: "The recompense for disobedience is weakness in worship, narrowness in livelihood, and difficulty in pleasure." It was said: "And what is difficulty in pleasure?" He said: "No lawful pleasure is met except that someone comes to spoil it for him."

He, exalted is He, mentions the prosperity and blessings they enjoyed, the pleasant and abundant life, the fertile lands, the secure places, and the villages that were connected and close to one another, with abundant trees, crops and fruit. Their traveler did not need to carry provisions or water. Wherever he stopped, he found water and fruit. He could rest at midday in one village and spend the night in another, according to what they needed on their journey. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We placed between them and the cities that We had blessed, visible cities﴾. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "They are villages in Sana'a." Abu Malik said the same.

Mujahid, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and others [[In T: "and other than them"]] said: it means the villages of al-Sham (Greater Syria), meaning that they used to travel from Yemen to al-Sham through apparent, connected villages.

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "The cities that We had blessed" [[In T: "are"]] are Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

Al-'Awfi also reported from him: "They are Arab villages between Madinah and al-Sham."

﴿Visible﴾ means clear and evident, known to travelers, who rested at midday in one and spent the night in another. For this reason He said: ﴿And We measured therein the travel﴾, meaning We arranged it according to what travelers need, ﴿Travel therein by night and by day, secure﴾, meaning security was assured for them in their travel by night and by day.

﴿But they said: "Our Lord, make the distance between our journeys longer," and they wronged themselves﴾. Others read: "Ba'ida (make distant) between our journeys." This was because they became ungrateful for this blessing, as Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and others said, and they loved deserts and wastelands in which crossing requires provisions, mounts, and travel through scorching heat and dangers. This is like the request of the Children of Israel to Musa that God bring forth for them from what the earth grows: its herbs, cucumbers, garlic, lentils and onions, even though they were living in a pleasant life with manna and quails, and with whatever food, drink and fine garments they desired. For this reason he said to them: ﴿Would you exchange that which is lower for that which is better? Go down to a city, for indeed you will have what you ask.﴾ And humiliation and poverty were struck upon them, and they returned with anger from Allah [al-Baqarah 2:61]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And how many a city have We destroyed which exulted in its livelihood﴾ [al-Qasas 28:58]. He, exalted is He, also said: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a city that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it in abundance from every place, but it denied the favors of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl 16:112].

Concerning these people He said: ﴿And they wronged themselves﴾, meaning through their disbelief, ﴿So We made them as narrations and tore them into complete dispersal﴾, meaning We made them a tale for people and a topic of conversation, [telling] of their news and how Allah plotted against them, and [how] He scattered their unity after gathering, harmony and pleasant living. They were dispersed throughout the lands, here and there. For this reason the Arabs say of a people when they scatter: "They scattered like the hands of Saba'" and "Ayadi Saba'," and "They scattered in every direction (shadhar madhar)." [[In T: "wa madar"]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan told us, Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid told us, I heard my father say: I heard [[In T: "And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated with his chain to 'Ikrimah"]] 'Ikrimah narrate the account of the people of Saba', saying: ﴿There was for Saba' in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and on the left﴾ up to His words ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim﴾. There were soothsayers among them, and the devils used to eavesdrop, and they informed the soothsayers of something from the news of the heavens. There was among them a noble soothsayer, rich in wealth, who was informed that their rule was about to end and that punishment had come close to them. He did not know what to do, because he had much wealth in property. He said to one of his sons, who was the most honored of them through his maternal uncles: "When tomorrow comes and I order you to do something, do not do it. When I scold you, scold me back, and when I strike you, slap me." He said: "O father, do not do it, for this is a great matter and a severe one." He said: "My son, a matter has occurred that cannot be avoided." He kept at him until he complied with that. When morning came and the people gathered, he said: "My son, do such and such." He refused, so his father scolded him, and he answered him back, and this went on between them until his father struck him. He leapt upon his father and slapped him. The father said: "My son slaps me? Bring me the blade." They said: "What will you do with the blade?" He said: "I will slaughter him." They said: "You will slaughter your son? Slap him, or do whatever you wish." He refused. They sent for his maternal uncles and informed them of this. His maternal uncles came and said: "Take from us whatever you wish." He refused except to slaughter him. They said: "Then you will die before you slaughter him." He said: "If the matter is like this, then I do not think I should remain in a land where my son and I are prevented from one another. Buy my houses, buy my land." He kept at it until he sold his houses, his land and his property. When the price was in his hand and he had secured it, he said: "O people, the punishment has come close to you and the end of your rule is near. Whoever among you wants a new home, a strong camel and a distant journey, let him join Oman. Whoever among you wants wine, dates [khamir] and juice [I did not memorize the word]—let him join Busra. Whoever among you wants the firmly rooted in mud, the ones who feed in drought, the ones who remain in the shallows, let him join Yathrib of the palm trees." His people obeyed him. The people of Oman went to Oman, Ghassan went to Busra, and the Aws and Khazraj and the Banu 'Uthman went to Yathrib of the palm trees. He said: They came to Batn Marr, and the Banu 'Uthman said: "This is a good place, we will not seek a replacement for it." So they stayed there, and they were named Khuza'ah for this reason, because they separated (inkhaza'u) from their companions. The Aws and Khazraj remained until they settled in Madinah, the people of Oman headed to Oman, and Ghassan headed to Busra.

This is a strange and wondrous report. This soothsayer was 'Amr ibn 'Amir, one of the leaders of Yemen and the great men of Saba' and their soothsayers [[In T: "their soothsayers"]].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned at the beginning of the Sirah what happened concerning 'Amr ibn 'Amir, who was the first to leave the lands of Yemen, because he sensed the sending of the 'Arim. He said: The reason 'Amr ibn 'Amir left Yemen—according to what Abu Zayd al-Ansari related to me—was that he saw a rat digging in the dam of Ma'rib, which used to hold back water from them, so that they directed it wherever they wished in their land. He knew that the dam could not last in this state, so he resolved to leave Yemen. He deceived his people: he ordered his youngest son, when he spoke harshly to him and struck him, to stand up and strike him back. The son did what he was ordered. 'Amr said: "I will not remain in a land where my face was struck by my youngest son." He displayed his wealth, and some nobles of Yemen said: "Seize the opportunity of 'Amr's anger." They bought his property, and he moved with his children and his grandchildren. The Azd said: "We will not stay behind 'Amr ibn 'Amir." They sold their property and left with him. They journeyed until they settled in the land of 'Akk, passing through and seeking lands. 'Akk fought them, and their war was back and forth. Concerning this 'Abbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami said:

"And 'Akk ibn 'Adnan, who prevailed
over Ghassan, until they were driven out from every place."

This verse is from a qasidah of his.

He said: Then they departed from them and scattered throughout the lands. The family of Jafnah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Amir settled in al-Sham. The Aws and Khazraj settled in Yathrib. Khuza'ah settled in Marr. The Azd of al-Sarah settled in al-Sarah, and the Azd of 'Oman settled in 'Oman. Then Allah sent the flood upon the dam and it collapsed, and concerning this Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed these verses.

Al-Suddi also mentioned the story of 'Amr ibn 'Amir in a manner similar to what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned, except that he said "he ordered his nephew" instead of "his son," up to his words "he sold his property and set out with his family, and they scattered." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah informed us [[Addition from T and al-Tabari]], from Ibn Ishaq, who said: They claim that 'Amr ibn 'Amir—and he was the uncle of the people—was a soothsayer, and he saw in his divination that his people would be torn apart and their journeys would be distanced. He said to them: "I know that you will be torn apart. Whoever among you has a far-reaching concern, a strong camel and a new water-skin, let him join Kas or Karud." He said: So Wada'ah ibn 'Amr went there. "And whoever among you has a heavy concern and a pressing matter, let him join the land of Shan." So 'Awf ibn 'Amr went there, and they are the ones called Bariq. "And whoever among you wants a comfortable life and a safe sanctuary, let him join al-Arzin." So Khuza'ah went there. "And whoever among you wants the firmly rooted in mud, the ones who feed in drought, let him join Yathrib of the palm trees." So the Aws and Khazraj went there, and they are the two tribes of the Ansar. "And whoever among you wants wine, dates, gold, silk, kingship and command, let him join Kuthi and Busra." So Ghassan, the Banu Jafnah, became the kings of al-Sham. "And whoever among them is in Iraq." Ibn Ishaq said: I have heard some people of knowledge say: This statement was only made by Tarifah, the wife of 'Amr ibn 'Amir, who was a soothsayer. She saw this in her divination. Allah knows best which of these was the case. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (22/59)]]

Sa'id reported from Qatadah, from al-Sha'bi: As for Ghassan, they joined al-Sham; as for the Ansar, they joined Yathrib; as for Khuza'ah, they joined Tihamah; and as for the Azd, they joined Oman. So Allah tore them into complete dispersal. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

Then Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abu 'Ubaydah told me, he said: al-A'sha, A'sha Banu Qays ibn Tha'labah, whose name was Maymun ibn Qays, said:

"And in that is an example for the one who takes warning,
and Ma'rib, over which the 'Arim has passed.

A dam that the Himyar built for them;
when its water came, it was not stopped.

It irrigated their crops and their vines,
though their water was abundant, when it was divided.

So they became dispersed, not able
to drink from it even as a weaned child."
[[Sirah of Ibn Hisham (1/14)]]

* * *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful person﴾ means: indeed, in what befell these people of vengeance and punishment, and the change of blessing and the transformation of well-being, there is a punishment for what they committed of disbelief and sins, a lesson and an indication for every servant who is patient over calamities and grateful for blessings.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman and Abd al-Razzaq al-Ma'ni narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Ayzar ibn Huraith, from Umar ibn Sa'd, from his father, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am amazed at the decree of Allah the Exalted for the believer. If good befalls him, he praises his Lord and gives thanks. If a calamity befalls him, he praises his Lord and endures patiently. The believer is rewarded for everything, even for the morsel he raises to his wife's mouth."

It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i in *al-Yawm wal-Layla*, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, with this chain. It is a ḥadīth ʿazīz (a hadith transmitted through two or more chains of narration) from the narration of Umar ibn Sa'd, from his father. There is also a corroborating report (shāhid) for it in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer! Allah does not decree anything for him except that it is good for him. If prosperity reaches him, he is thankful, and that is good for him; if adversity reaches him, he is patient, and that is good for him. And this is not so for anyone except the believer."

(I have not found it from the hadith of Abu Hurairah in this form. It was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2999), from the hadith of Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him.)

* * *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for every patient, grateful person﴾ means: indeed, in what befell these people of vengeance and punishment, and the change of blessing and the transformation of well-being, there is a punishment for what they committed of disbelief and sins, a lesson and an indication for every servant who is patient over calamities and grateful for blessings.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman and Abd al-Razzaq al-Ma'ni narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Ayzar ibn Huraith, from Umar ibn Sa'd, from his father, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am amazed at the decree of Allah the Exalted for the believer. If good befalls him, he praises his Lord and gives thanks. If a calamity befalls him, he praises his Lord and endures patiently. The believer is rewarded for everything, even for the morsel he raises to his wife's mouth."

It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i in *al-Yawm wal-Layla*, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, with this chain. It is a ḥadīth ʿazīz (a hadith transmitted through two or more chains of narration) from the narration of Umar ibn Sa'd, from his father. There is also a corroborating report (shāhid) for it in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer! Allah does not decree anything for him except that it is good for him. If prosperity reaches him, he is thankful, and that is good for him; if adversity reaches him, he is patient, and that is good for him. And this is not so for anyone except the believer."

(I have not found it from the hadith of Abu Hurairah in this form. It was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2999), from the hadith of Suhayb, may Allah be pleased with him.)

ʿAbd said: Yunus narrated to us, from Shaiban, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person﴾: Mutarrif used to say: "What an excellent servant is the steadfast and grateful one, who gives thanks when he is given, and endures patiently when he is tested."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 34, verse 20–21:

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the story of Saba' and what they did in following their desires and Satan, He informed about them and about others like them who followed Iblis and desire and opposed guidance and right direction. He said: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: This verse is like His saying, reporting about Iblis when he refused to prostrate to Adam, then he said: ﴿Have you seen this one whom You have honored over me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control of his descendants, except for a few﴾ [al-Isra' 17:62], then he said: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful﴾ [al-A'raf 7:17]. And the verses on this are many.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: When Allah sent Adam down from the Garden, and Hawwa' was with him, Iblis also descended, rejoicing at what he had obtained from the two of them, and he said: "If I have obtained from the two parents what I have obtained, then the offspring are weaker and weaker." That was an assumption from Iblis, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a group of the believers﴾. At that, Iblis said: "I will not leave the son of Adam as long as the spirit is in him. I will mislead him, make him hope, and deceive him." Allah said: "By My might, I will not withhold repentance from him as long as he does not gasp in death, and he will not call upon Me except that I respond to him, he will not ask Me except that I give him, and he will not seek forgiveness from Me except that I forgive him." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And he had no authority over them﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, no proof.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: By Allah, he did not strike them with a staff, nor did he compel them to anything; it was only deception and false hopes with which he called them, and they responded to him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿But that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt concerning it﴾, that is: We only empowered him over them so that the matter of the one who believes in the Hereafter, its resurrection, reckoning and recompense, might become manifest, so that he would worship his Lord, mighty and majestic, well in this world, from among those who are in doubt concerning it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾, that is: along with His guarding, whoever went astray followed Iblis, and by His guarding and protection whoever was safe among the believers, followers of the messengers, was kept safe.

As for His saying: ﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾, that is: along with His guarding, whoever went astray followed Iblis, and by His guarding and protection whoever was safe among the believers, followers of the messengers, was kept safe.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah, may He be exalted, explains that He is the One God, the Unique, the Eternal, the Self-Sufficient, who has no equal and no partner. Rather, He alone is independent in His command, with no sharer, no rival, and no opponent. He said: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claim besides Allah﴾, that is, from among the deities that were worshipped besides Him, ﴿who own not an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth﴾. This is like His statement, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And those you call upon besides Him own not even a date-seed's membrane﴾ [Fatir: 13].

* *

His statement, ﴿And they have no share in them﴾, means they do not own anything independently or as a partner. ﴿Nor is there for Him any helper among them﴾, means that among these rivals there is no supporter from whom He seeks aid in affairs. Rather, all creation is in need of Him and are His servants.

Qatadah said concerning His statement, ﴿Nor is there for Him any helper among them﴾: "No one who helps Him with anything."

He said: ﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He permits﴾, that is, because of His greatness, majesty and magnificence, no one dares to intercede with Him, may He be exalted, in anything except after He has given permission for the intercession, as He said: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. He also said: ﴿And how many an angel in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾ [an-Najm: 26]. And He said: ﴿And they intercede not except for one whom He approves, and they are, out of fear of Him, apprehensive﴾ [al-Anbiya': 28].

For this reason it is established in the two Sahihs, through more than one chain from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who is the master of the children of Adam and the greatest intercessor with Allah, that when he stands in the Praiseworthy Station to intercede for all creation, so that He may come to their Lord for the judgment to be decided, he said: "I will prostrate to Allah, and He will leave me as long as He wills to leave me, and He will open for me praises that I cannot count right now. Then it will be said: 'O Muhammad, raise your head, speak and you will be heard, ask and you will be given, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted.'" (The hadith in full.)

* *

His statement: ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts, they say: "What has your Lord said?" They say: "The truth."﴾ This is also a station of lofty greatness. When Allah speaks with the revelation, the inhabitants of the heavens hear His speech and tremble from awe, until something like a swoon overtakes them. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, Masruq and others.

﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾, that is, the fear has departed from them. Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan and Qatadah said concerning His statement, ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾: "It means it was dispelled from their hearts." Some of the early scholars read it, and it is also reported as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report: "Until, when it is emptied (furrigha)" with the ghayn (the dotted letter), and it returns to the first meaning.

When this is the case, they ask one another: "What has your Lord said?" Then the bearers of the Throne inform those nearest to them, then those nearest to them inform those beneath them, until the report reaches the inhabitants of the lowest heaven. For this reason He said: ﴿They say: "The truth,"﴾ that is, they report what He said without addition or subtraction, ﴿and He is the Most High, the Great﴾.

Others said: rather, the meaning of His statement, ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾, refers to the polytheists at the time of death, and on the Day of Resurrection when they awaken from the heedlessness they were in during the world, and their minds return to them on the Day of Resurrection. They say: "What has your Lord said?" It is said to them: "The truth," and they are informed of what they were heedless of in the world.

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾: "He uncovers the veil from them on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Hasan said: ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾ means what is in them of doubt and denial. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾ means what is in them of doubt. He said: "The devil is removed from their hearts and departs from them, along with their wishful thinking and what used to mislead them. ﴿They say: 'What has your Lord said?' They say: 'The truth, and He is the Most High, the Great.'" He said: "And this is about the children of Adam, at the time of death; they acknowledge it when acknowledgment no longer benefits them."

Ibn Jarir preferred the first view, that the pronoun refers to the angels. This is the truth about which there is no doubt, because of the soundness of the hadiths and reports concerning it. We shall mention a portion of them which indicates the others:

Al-Bukhari said, when explaining this noble verse in his Sahih: "Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, 'Amr narrated to us, I heard 'Ikrimah say, I heard Abu Hurayrah say that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When Allah decrees a matter in the heaven, the angels strike their wings in submission to His word, like a chain on a smooth rock. When fear is removed from their hearts, they say: "What has your Lord said?" They say: "The truth, and He is the Most High, the Great." Then the eavesdroppers hear it, and the eavesdroppers are one above another'—Sufyan described it with his hand, spreading and separating his fingers—'so they hear the word and convey it to those beneath them, and then the next conveys it to the one beneath him, until it is conveyed to the tongue of the sorcerer or the soothsayer. Sometimes the meteor overtakes him before he conveys it, and sometimes he conveys it before the meteor overtakes him, and he tells a hundred lies with it, and it is said: "Did he not tell us on such and such a day such and such?" and he is believed because of that one word that was heard from heaven.'"

Al-Bukhari alone reported it from this route, not Muslim. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain.

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: "Muhammad ibn Ja'far and 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, al-Zuhri informed us, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with a group of his companions—'Abd al-Razzaq said: 'from the Ansar'—when a star fell and shone brightly. He said: 'What did you used to say when such a thing happened in the Jahiliyyah?' They said: 'We used to say: a great person is born, or a great person dies.'" I said to al-Zuhri: "Was it thrown in the Jahiliyyah?" He said: "Yes, but it became more intense when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not thrown for the death of anyone or for the life of anyone. But when our Lord, blessed and exalted, decrees a matter, the bearers of the Throne glorify Him, then the inhabitants of the heaven nearest to them glorify, until the glorification reaches this lowest heaven. Then the inhabitants of the heaven nearest to the bearers of the Throne ask the bearers of the Throne: 'What has your Lord said?' They inform them, and the inhabitants of each heaven inform the heaven beneath, until the report reaches this heaven. The jinn snatch the hearing and are struck, and whatever they bring as it is, is true, but they distort it and add to it."

This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Muslim also reported it in his Sahih, from the hadith of Salih ibn Kaysan, al-Awza'i, Yunus and Ma'mar ibn 'Ubayd Allah, four of them from al-Zuhri, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn 'Abbas, from a man from the Ansar, with the same wording. Yunus said: "from men of the Ansar." Likewise al-Nasa'i reported it in his "Tafsir" from the hadith of al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri, with the same wording. al-Tirmidhi reported it from al-Husayn ibn Hurayth, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from al-Awza'i, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from a man from the Ansar, may Allah be pleased with him. And Allah knows best.

Another hadith: Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Muhammad ibn 'Awf and Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn Sayyar al-Ramadi narrated to us—the wording is that of Muhammad ibn 'Awf—they both said: Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, al-Walid—that is Ibn Muslim—narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Zakariyya, from Raja' ibn Haywah, from al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When Allah wishes to reveal a command, He speaks with the revelation. When He speaks, the heavens are seized by a violent quaking, or he said a violent trembling, out of fear of Allah. When the inhabitants of the heavens hear that, they swoon and fall prostrate to Allah. The first to raise his head will be Jibril, and Allah speaks to him from His revelation with what He wills. Then Jibril passes with it over the angels. Every time he passes a heaven, its angels ask him: "What has our Lord said, O Jibril?" He says: "He said the truth, and He is the Most High, the Great." Then they all say what Jibril said, and Jibril brings the revelation to where Allah commands him, from the heaven and the earth.'"

Likewise Ibn Jarir and Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it, from Zakariyya ibn Aban al-Misri, from Nu'aym ibn Hammad, with the same wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I heard my father say: This hadith is not in Syria from al-Walid ibn Muslim." May Allah have mercy on him.

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated, from al-'Awfi, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Qatadah, that they both explained this verse as referring to the beginning of Allah's revelation to Muhammad (ﷺ) after the interval (al-fatrah) that was between him and 'Isa. There is no doubt that this is more fitting to be included in this verse.

Rather, He alone is independent in His command, with no sharer, no rival, and no opponent.
