Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about the persistence of the disbelievers in their transgression, obstinacy, and insistence on not believing in the Qur'an and in what it reports concerning the Return (al-ma'ad). Therefore He said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "We will never believe in this Qur'an, nor in that which came before it."﴾ Allah, exalted is He, says, threatening and warning them, and informing about their humiliating positions before Him during their dispute and argumentation: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, [how] they refer back [their] words to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers."﴾ That is, "Were it not for you preventing us, we would have followed the messengers and believed in what they brought to us." Then the leaders and masters, who are the ones who were arrogant, will say to them: ﴿Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals.﴾ That is, "We did not do to you more than that we called you, and you followed us without any proof or evidence, and you opposed the proofs, the evidences, and the arguments that the prophets brought, out of your own desires and your choosing of that."

Therefore they said: ﴿Rather, you were criminals.﴾ ﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, [it was] the plotting of [you] by night and day,"﴾ That is, "Rather, you used to plot against us night and day, deceiving us, giving us false hopes, and telling us that we were upon guidance and upon something [of truth], whereas all of that was falsehood, lies, and fabrication."

Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿the plotting of night and day﴾: it means their plotting by night and by day. Likewise Malik said, from Zayd ibn Aslam: their plotting by night and by day.

﴿When you commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him﴾ — that is, equals and deities along with Him, and you set up for us doubts and impossible things by which you misled us. ﴿And they will conceal regret when they see the punishment.﴾ That is, all of them, leaders and followers alike, each regretted what had passed from him.

﴿And We will put shackles around the necks of those who disbelieved.﴾ These are the chains that join their hands with their necks. ﴿Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ That is, "We only recompense you for your deeds, each according to his measure: the leaders have a punishment according to their measure, and the followers according to theirs." ﴿[Allah] will say, "For each is double, but you do not know."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 38]

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 34, verses 34–39:

Allah, exalted is He, says, consoling His Prophet and commanding him to take as an example those messengers who came before him. He informs him that He never sent a prophet to any town without its affluent people (*mutrafun*) denying him, while its weak followed him. As the people of Noah said: ﴿Shall we believe you when the lowest of people follow you?﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 111], and ﴿We see that only the lowest of us, those who are hasty in judgment, follow you﴾ [Hud: 27]. The leaders of the people of Salih said to those among them who were oppressed and had believed: ﴿Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?﴾ They said: ﴿We believe in what he has been sent with.﴾ Those who were arrogant said: ﴿We disbelieve in what you believe﴾ [Al-A'raf: 75–76]. Allah also says: ﴿Thus We have tried some of them by means of others, that they may say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [Al-An'am: 53]. And He says: ﴿Thus We placed in every town its greatest criminals, that they might plot therein﴾ [Al-An'am: 123]. And He says: ﴿When We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they commit sin therein, and the word becomes due against it﴾ [Al-Isra: 16]. Here He says: ﴿We did not send a warner to a town but its affluent ones said﴾, meaning, a prophet or a messenger, ﴿"Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ The affluent (*mutrafun*) are those who possess blessings, pomp, wealth and leadership.

Qatadah said: They are their tyrants, their leaders and the heads of evil among them. ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾, meaning, we do not believe in it and do not follow it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Harun ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: There were two partners, one of whom went out to the coast while the other remained. When the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, the one who had gone wrote to his companion asking him: "What has happened?" He wrote back to him that no one from Quraysh had followed him, only the lowest of the people and their poor had followed him. He said: So he abandoned his trade and went to his companion and said: "Show me to him." He said: And he (the companion) used to read the scriptures, or some of the scriptures. So he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "To what do you call?" He said: "To such and such." He said: "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "And what is your knowledge of that?" He said: "No prophet has been sent except that the lowest of the people and their poor have followed him." He said: Then this verse was revealed: ﴿We did not send a warner to a town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ and the verses that follow. He said: Then the Prophet (ﷺ) sent to him: "Indeed Allah has sent down the confirmation of what you said." [Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it as in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/704), but in al-Durr it says "Ibn Zayd" instead of "Abu Razin".]

Likewise Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan when he asked him those questions. Among what he said: "And I asked you: Do the weak of the people follow him, or their nobles? You claimed: Rather, its weak. And they are the followers of the messengers."

* *

Allah's statement, informing about the affluent deniers: ﴿They said: "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾ That is, they boasted of the abundance of wealth and children, and they believed that this was evidence of Allah's love for them and His concern for them, and that He would not give them this in this world and then punish them in the Hereafter. But that is far from them. Allah says: ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children is hastening for them good things? Nay, they do not perceive﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 55–56]. He also says: ﴿So do not let their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them with them in the worldly life, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾ [At-Tawbah: 55]. And Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Leave Me with the one whom I created alone. And I gave him extensive wealth, and children present with him, and I made things easy for him. Then he desires that I should increase. No! Indeed, he was stubborn toward Our verses. I will overwhelm him with a steep ascent﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 11–17].

Allah has informed us about the owner of those two gardens: that he possessed wealth, children and fruit, yet they did not avail him anything, rather all of that was stripped from him in this world before the Hereafter. Therefore, Allah, exalted is He, says here: ﴿Say: "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it."﴾ That is, He gives wealth to whom He loves and to whom He does not love. He makes poor whom He wills and makes rich whom He wills, and to Him belongs perfect and far-reaching wisdom and conclusive, decisive proof. ﴿But most of the people do not know.﴾

Then He said: ﴿And it is not your wealth or your children that bring you near to Us in position﴾, meaning, these are not evidence of Our love for you or Our concern for you.

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Kathir narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, Yazid ibn al-Asamm narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah does not look at your forms or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds." It was related by Muslim and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Kathir ibn Hisham, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, with it. [Al-Musnad (2/539), Sahih Muslim no. (2564), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4143).]

Therefore He said: ﴿Except for one who believes and does righteous work﴾, meaning, what brings you near to Us in position is only faith and righteous deeds. ﴿For those will be a double reward for what they did﴾, meaning, their good deed is multiplied by ten like its amount, up to seven hundred times. ﴿And they will be safe in the upper chambers﴾, meaning, safe in the high dwellings of Paradise, secure from every harm, fear and injury, and from every evil that is to be feared.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father narrated to us, Farwah ibn Abi al-Maghra' al-Kindi narrated to us, al-Qasim and 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed in Paradise there are chambers whose outsides can be seen from their insides, and whose insides can be seen from their outsides." A Bedouin asked: "For whom are they?" He said: "For those who speak good words, feed food, persist in fasting, and pray at night while people are sleeping." [Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan no. (1984) through 'Ali ibn Mushir from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq with a longer version, and he said: "This is a gharib (strange) hadith, we do not know it except from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, and the scholars of hadith have spoken about this 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq because of his memory, and he is Kufan." I say: It has supporting reports from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, Abu Malik al-Ash'ari and Abu Mu'anig al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with them.]

﴿And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them﴾, meaning, they strive to turn people away from the way of Allah, from following the messengers, and from believing in His verses. ﴿Those will be brought forth into punishment﴾, meaning, all of them will be recompensed for their deeds therein according to what they deserve.

* *

His statement: ﴿Say: "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him."﴾ That is, according to what He has of wisdom in that. He extends much wealth to this one, and restricts and greatly constricts the provision of that one. He has in that wisdom which no one else perceives, as He said: ﴿See how We have favored some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference﴾ [Al-Isra: 21]. That is, just as they differ in this world, one being a destitute pauper and another being a wealthy one who is given abundance, so too in the Hereafter: this one is in the upper chambers, in the highest ranks, and that one is in the depths, in the lowest levels of Hell. And the best of people in this world, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed he has succeeded who has embraced Islam, was given sustenance sufficient for him, and Allah made him content with what He gave him." Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn 'Amr. [Sahih Muslim no. (1054).]

* *

His statement: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾, meaning, whatever you spend of anything in what He has commanded you and permitted for you, He will replace it for you in this world through a substitute, and in the Hereafter through recompense and reward. As established in the hadith: Allah, exalted is He, says: "Spend, O son of Adam, and I will spend upon you." [Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih no. (4684) and Muslim in his Sahih no. (993), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] And in the hadith: Two angels call out every day, one of them says: "O Allah, give the one who withholds a loss," and the other says: "O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement." [Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih no. (1442) and Muslim in his Sahih no. (1010), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Spend, Bilal, and do not fear from the Lord of the Throne poverty." [This has come from a group of the Companions. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/340) through Qays ibn al-Rabi' from Abu Husayn, from Yahya ibn Wathhab, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and Qays ibn al-Rabi' has been declared weak. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/342), Abu Ya'la in his Musnad (10/429) and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (2/280) from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/359) through Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, from Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, and in it is Ibn Zabalah, who is weak.]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Aziz al-Tallas: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Kawthar ibn Hakim, from Makhul, who said: It reached me from Hudhayfah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, after your time there will be a biting era, in which the wealthy man bites on what is in his hand out of fear of spending." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr (6/707) and said: "Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with a weak chain, and he mentioned it."]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili narrated: Rawh ibn Hatim narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Kawthar ibn Hakim, from Makhul, who said: It reached me from Hudhayfah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, after this time of yours there will be a biting era, in which the wealthy man bites on what is in his hands out of fear of spending." Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾. And the worst of creation will drink from it, selling to every distressed person. Indeed, the sale of the distressed is forbidden. [Indeed, the sale of the distressed is forbidden.] The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him nor forsake him. If you have a kindness, then extend it to your brother, and otherwise do not increase him in his ruin."

This is a gharib (strange) hadith from this route, and in its chain there is weakness. [Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (1/261) and attributed it to Abu Ya'la in his Musnad.]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Yunus al-Hasan ibn Yazid, who said: Mujahid said: Let none of you interpret this verse: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾ to mean: if one of you has what sustains him, let him be moderate in it, for provision is apportioned.

Qatadah said: They are their tyrants, their leaders and the heads of evil among them. ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with﴾, meaning, we do not believe in it and do not follow it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Harun ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, who said: There were two partners, one of whom went out to the coast while the other remained. When the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, the one who had gone wrote to his companion asking him: "What has happened?" He wrote back to him that no one from Quraysh had followed him, only the lowest of the people and their poor had followed him. He said: So he abandoned his trade and went to his companion and said: "Show me to him." He said: And he (the companion) used to read the scriptures, or some of the scriptures. So he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "To what do you call?" He said: "To such and such." He said: "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." He said: "And what is your knowledge of that?" He said: "No prophet has been sent except that the lowest of the people and their poor have followed him." He said: Then this verse was revealed: ﴿We did not send a warner to a town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ and the verses that follow. A Bedouin asked: "For whom are they?" He said: "For those who speak good words, feed food, persist in fasting, and pray at night while people are sleeping." [Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan no. Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/359) through Abu Ishaq, from Masruq, from Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, and in it is Ibn Zabalah, who is weak.]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Aziz al-Tallas: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Kawthar ibn Hakim, from Makhul, who said: It reached me from Hudhayfah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, after your time there will be a biting era, in which the wealthy man bites on what is in his hand out of fear of spending." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr (6/707) and said: "Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with a weak chain, and he mentioned it."]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili narrated: Rawh ibn Hatim narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Kawthar ibn Hakim, from Makhul, who said: It reached me from Hudhayfah that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, after this time of yours there will be a biting era, in which the wealthy man bites on what is in his hands out of fear of spending." Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾. And the worst of creation will drink from it, selling to every distressed person. Indeed, the sale of the distressed is forbidden. [Indeed, the sale of the distressed is forbidden.] The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him nor forsake him. If you have a kindness, then extend it to your brother, and otherwise do not increase him in his ruin."

This is a gharib (strange) hadith from this route, and in its chain there is weakness. [Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (1/261) and attributed it to Abu Ya'la in his Musnad.]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Yunus al-Hasan ibn Yazid, who said: Mujahid said: Let none of you interpret this verse: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾ to mean: if one of you has what sustains him, let him be moderate in it, for provision is apportioned.

Allah, may He be exalted, informs that on the Day of Resurrection He will rebuke the polytheists before all of creation. He will ask the angels, whom the polytheists claimed they worshipped as rivals (andad) to Allah, being in the form of angels, so that these would bring them near to Allah in closeness (zulfa). He will say to the angels: ﴿Did these used to worship you?﴾ That is, did you order them to worship you? As He said in Surah al-Furqan: ﴿Did you lead astray these servants of Mine, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾ [al-Furqan: 17]. And as He will say to Jesus: ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?" He will say, "Glory be to You! It was not for me to say what I have no right to say."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116]. Likewise the angels will say: ﴿Glory be to You!﴾ That is, You are exalted and sanctified above having any god with You. ﴿You are our Protector, not them.﴾ That is, we are Your servants, and we disassociate ourselves from them before You. ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn,﴾ meaning the devils (shayatin), because they are the ones who adorned for them the worship of idols and led them astray. ﴿Most of them were believers in them.﴾ As Allah said: ﴿They invoke besides Him only females, and they invoke only a rebellious devil.﴾ [an-Nisa: 117].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So today, none of you will have power to benefit or harm another.﴾ That is, no benefit will reach you from those whose benefit you hoped for today from the rivals and idols, whose worship you stored up for your calamities and distresses. Today they possess no power to benefit you or harm you. ﴿And We will say to those who wronged﴾ — they are the polytheists — ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ That is, it will be said to them, as rebuke and reproach.

Allah, exalted is He, informs about the disbelievers that they deserve from Him punishment and painful torment, because whenever His clear verses were recited to them, they heard them fresh and new from the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿They said, "This is none but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship."﴾ They mean that the religion of their fathers is the truth, and that what the Messenger brought them is false—may the curse of Allah be upon them and upon their fathers. ﴿And they said, "This is none but a fabricated lie."﴾ They mean the Qur'an. ﴿And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them, "This is nothing but evident magic."﴾

Allah says: ﴿And We had not given them any scriptures that they could study, nor had We sent to them before you any warner.﴾ That is, Allah had not sent down to the Arabs any book before the Qur'an, nor had He sent to them any prophet before Muhammad (ﷺ). They used to wish for this and would say: "If a warner came to us, or a book were sent down to us, we would surely be better guided than others." But when Allah bestowed this favour upon them, they denied him, opposed him and rejected him.

Then He said: ﴿And those before them denied, and they did not reach even a tenth of what We had given them.﴾ That is, of the nations. Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, of strength in this world. Qatadah, as-Suddi and Ibn Zayd also said the same. As Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We had certainly established them in that wherein We have not established you, and We gave them hearing and sight and hearts, but their hearing and their sight and their hearts did not avail them anything, since they were rejecting the signs of Allah; and there encompassed them that which they had been mocking.﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 26] ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in number and greater in strength.﴾ [Ghafir: 82] That is, that did not avert from them the punishment of Allah, nor did it repel it. Rather, Allah destroyed them when they denied His messengers. For this reason He said: ﴿So they denied My messengers, and how was My reprisal?﴾ That is, how was My punishment, My retribution and My vindication of My messengers?

Allah says: Say, O Muhammad, to these disbelievers who claim that you are mad: "I only admonish you with one thing" — i.e., I only command you with one thing — which is: "that you stand up for Allah in pairs and individually, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion" (﴿أَنْ تَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ مَثْنَى وَفُرَادَى ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُوا مَا بِصَاحِبِكُمْ مِنْ جِنَّةٍ﴾). That is, stand up sincerely for Allah, free from desire and partisanship, so that some of you ask one another: "Is there madness in Muhammad?" Then some of you advise others. "Then reflect" means: a man looks into the matter of Muhammad ﷺ for himself, and asks others among the people about his affair if it is unclear to him, and reflects upon that. For this reason He said: "that you stand up for Allah in pairs and individually, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion."

This is the meaning reported by Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Suddi, Qatadah and others, and this is what is meant by the verse.

As for the hadith narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: "My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Sadaqah ibn Khalid narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'Atikah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: 'I have been given three things that were not given to anyone before me, and it is no boast: spoils of war were made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for those before me, who used to gather their spoils and burn them. I was sent to every red and black person, whereas every prophet was sent only to his own people. The earth was made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification; I perform tayammum with clean earth and pray wherever the prayer overtakes me. Allah said: "that you stand up for Allah in pairs and individually." And I was aided with awe (al-Ru'b) a month's journey ahead of me.'" This hadith has a weak chain of narration, and interpreting the verse as referring to standing in prayer in congregation and individually is far-fetched. It is likely that this was inserted into the hadith by one of the narrators, for its origin is established in the Sahihs and elsewhere [[The hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, in the two Sahihs was previously cited under the commentary on verse 28 of this surah.]]. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿إِنْ هُوَ إِلا نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾ ("He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment"), al-Bukhari narrated here:

Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Khazim narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: One day the Prophet ﷺ climbed al-Safa and said: "Yā ṣabāḥāh!" (a cry of alarm). The Quraysh gathered around him and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "Tell me, if I informed you that an enemy would attack you in the morning or in the evening, would you not believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." Abu Lahab said: "Ruin to you! Did you gather us for this?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾ [al-Masad]. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4801).]]

This was mentioned previously under His saying: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 214].

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Bashir ibn al-Muhajir narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Buraydah narrated to me, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us one day and called out three times, then said: "O people, do you know what my example and your example are?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "My example and your example are like a people who feared an enemy coming upon them, so they sent a man to watch for them. While he was thus, he saw the enemy, and he came hurrying to warn them, but he feared the enemy would reach him before he could warn his people, so he waved his garment: 'O people, you have been overtaken! O people, you have been overtaken!' — three times."

By this same chain the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I and the Hour have been sent together, and it nearly outran me." Imam Ahmad alone narrated it in his Musnad. [[al-Musnad (5/348).]]

Allah says, commanding His Messenger to say to the polytheists: ﴿Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours.﴾ That is, I do not want from you any wage or gift in return for conveying Allah's Message to you, for giving you my counsel, and for commanding you to worship Allah. ﴿My reward is only from Allah.﴾ That is, I only seek the reward for that from Allah. ﴿And He is, over all things, Witness.﴾ That is, He is Knowing of all matters, including what I am upon in informing you that He has sent me to you, and what you are upon.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord casts the truth. Knower of the unseen."﴾ This is like His saying: ﴿He sends down the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. That is, He sends the angel to whomever He wills of His servants among the people of the earth, and He is Knower of the unseen, so nothing is hidden from Him in the heavens or on the earth.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate nor return."﴾ That is, the truth has come from Allah and the great Law, and falsehood has departed, perished and vanished, like His saying: ﴿Rather, We cast the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it is vanishing﴾ [Al-Anbya': 18]. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered al-Masjid al-Haram on the day of the Conquest and found those idols set up around the Ka'bah, he began to strike the idol with the tip of his bow, reciting: ﴿And say, "The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish."﴾ and ﴿Say, "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate nor return."﴾ Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i alone at this verse, all from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar 'Abdullah ibn Sakhbarah, from Ibn Mas'ud, with it.

That is, falsehood has no argument, no leadership, and no word left.

Qatadah and al-Suddi asserted that what is meant by falsehood here is Iblis, that he does not create anyone nor restore anyone, and he has no power over that. Although this is true, it is not what is meant here, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, "If I go astray, I only go astray against myself; but if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me."﴾ That is, all good is from Allah, and in what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed of revelation and the manifest truth, in which there is guidance, clarification and right direction. Whoever goes astray, he only goes astray of his own accord, as 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said when he was asked about that issue concerning the mufawwidah (the one who gives a bride no dower): "I say about it according to my opinion; if it is correct, it is from Allah, and if it is wrong, it is from me and from Satan, and Allah and His Messenger are free of it." [See the report in al-Musnad (1/477).]

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Hearing, Near.﴾ That is, He hears the words of His servants, is Near, and answers the supplication of the one who calls upon Him. Al-Nasa'i has narrated here the hadith of Abu Musa, which is in the Two Sahihs, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, you do not call upon one who is deaf or absent; you call upon One who is Hearing, Near, Responsive." [Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (11427); Sahih al-Bukhari (4205); Sahih Muslim (2704).]

* *

Allah says: "If only you could see, O Muhammad, when these deniers are terrified on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and there will be no escape﴾, meaning there will be no way out for them, no refuge and no shelter, ﴿and they will be seized from a near place﴾, meaning they will not be able to flee; rather they will be seized from the very first moment."

Al-Hasan al-Basri (a leading early scholar of Basra) said: "When they come out of their graves."

Mujahid, 'Ata' al-'Awfi and Qatadah said: "From beneath their feet."

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak: "That is, their punishment in this world."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "That is, their killing on the Day of Badr."

The correct view is that what is meant by this is the Day of Resurrection, which is the great catastrophe, although what was mentioned is connected to it.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) related from some of them that he said: "What is meant by this is an army that will be swallowed up between Makkah and Madinah in the days of the Banu 'Abbas." Then he cited a hadith in this regard that is entirely fabricated, and he did not point this out. This is a strange and astonishing matter from him.

﴿And they will say, "We believe in Him"﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection they will say, "We believe in Allah and His Books and His Messengers," just as Allah says: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, saying, "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may act righteously; indeed we are certain."﴾ [As-Sajdah: 12]. Therefore Allah says: ﴿But how can they reach [that faith] from a distant place?﴾, meaning, how can they grasp faith when they have gone far from the place where it is accepted from them and have arrived at the Hereafter, which is the abode of recompense, not the abode of trial? Had they believed in this world, that would have benefited them, but after their arrival in the Hereafter there is no way for them to accept faith, just as there is no way to obtain a thing for one who reaches for it from far away.

Mujahid said: ﴿But how can they reach [that faith]?﴾ — he said: "Reaching for it."

Al-Zuhri said: "At-tanawush" is their reaching for faith while they are in the Hereafter, when the world has been cut off from them.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Indeed, they sought the matter from a place where it cannot be attained; they reached for faith from a distant place."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They sought a return to the world and repentance for what they were in, but it is not the time for return or repentance." Likewise Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said, may Allah have mercy on him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they had already disbelieved in it before﴾, meaning, how can faith be attained for them in the Hereafter when they disbelieved in the truth in the world and denied the Messengers?

﴿And they cast [their words] about the unseen from a distant place﴾: Malik related from Zayd ibn Aslam: "﴿And they cast about the unseen﴾" — he said: "By conjecture."

I say: As Allah says: ﴿guessing about the unseen﴾ [Al-Kahf: 22]. At one time they say: "He is a poet." At another: "He is a soothsayer." At another: "He is a sorcerer." At another: "He is insane." And so on through other false statements. They also deny the unseen: the Resurrection, the Gathering and the Return, and they say: ﴿We think only a thought, and we are not certain﴾ [Al-Jathiyah: 32].

Qatadah said: "They hurl guesses, with no resurrection, no Paradise and no Fire."

* *

His saying: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾: al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Dahhak and others said: "That is, faith."

Al-Suddi said: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ refers to repentance. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him.

Mujahid said: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ refers to the things of this world: wealth, adornment and family. This is also related from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar and al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and it is the view of al-Bukhari and a group. The correct position is that there is no contradiction between the two views, for a barrier has indeed been placed between them and their desires in the world, and between them and what they sought in the Hereafter, so they were prevented from it.

Ibn Abi Hatim has mentioned here a very strange, indeed extremely astonishing report, so we will mention it in full. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Bishr ibn Hujr al-Sami narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Mansur al-Anbari narrated to us, from al-Sharaqi ibn Qutami, from Sa'id ibn Tarif, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: There was a man from the Children of Israel who was prosperous — that is, Allah had opened wealth to him — and he died, and his worthless son inherited him — that is, corrupt — and he would spend the wealth of Allah on the disobedience of Allah. When the brothers of his father saw this, they came to the young man, blamed him and reproached him, so the young man became resentful and sold his property for cash, then travelled and came to a gushing spring, and he spent his wealth there and built a palace. One day as he was sitting, a wind carried to him a woman of the most beautiful face and the sweetest fragrance — that is, a scent — and she said: "Who are you, O servant of Allah?" He said: "I am a man from the Children of Israel." She said: "Is this palace yours, and this wealth?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Do you have a wife?" He said: "No." She said: "How can life be pleasant for you without a wife?" He said: "That was the case before." She said: "Do you have a husband?" She said: "No." He said: "Would you accept that I marry you?" She said: "I am a woman who is a mile away from you. When tomorrow comes, take provisions for a day and come to me, and if you see a terror on your way, let it not frighten you." When the next day came, he took provisions for a day and set out, until he reached a palace, and he knocked on its door, and a young man of the most beautiful face and the sweetest fragrance came out to him and said: "Who are you, O servant of Allah?" He said: "I am the Israelite." He said: "What is your need?" He said: "The mistress of this palace has invited me to herself." He said: "You have told the truth." He said: "Did you see anything terrifying on your way?" He said: "Yes, and had she not told me that there was no harm upon me, what I saw would have terrified me. I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a bitch with its mouth open. I was startled and leapt, and behold, I was behind her, and her puppies were barking in her belly." The young man said to him: "You will not understand this; this will happen at the end of time: a youth will sit with the elders in their assembly and will outdo them in speech."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a hundred ewes in full udder, and among them a kid that was sucking them; when it had reached them and thought it had left nothing, it opened its mouth seeking more. He said: "You will not understand this; this will happen at the end of time: a king will gather all the wealth of the people, and when he thinks he has left nothing, he will open his mouth seeking more."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a tree, and a branch of one of its trees pleased me because of its freshness, so I wanted to cut it, and another tree called out to me: "O servant of Allah, take from me!" Until all the trees called out together: "O servant of Allah, take from us!" He said: "You will not understand this; this will happen at the end of time: men will become few and women will become many, so that a man will propose to a woman and ten or twenty women will invite him to themselves."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a man standing over a spring, drawing water for each person; when they dispersed from him, he poured what was in his jug and nothing in his jug clung to anything of the water. He said: "You will not understand this; this will happen at the end of time: the storyteller will teach people knowledge and then will go against them into the disobedience of Allah."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a ewe, and behold, a people had taken hold of its legs, and a man had taken hold of its horns, and a man had taken hold of its tail, and a man had mounted it, and a man was milking it. He said: "As for the ewe, it is this world. Those who took hold of its legs are falling away from its life. As for the one who took hold of its horns, he struggles with distress from its life. As for the one who took hold of its tail, it has turned away from him. As for the one who mounted it, he has left it. As for the one who is milking it, well done, that has taken it away."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a man drawing from a well, and each time he brought out his bucket he poured it into a pool, and the water flowed back into the well. He said: "This is a man whom Allah has rejected his righteous deed, and He did not accept it."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a man sowing seed, which then ripens, and behold, good wheat. He said: "This is a man whose righteous deed Allah has accepted, and He has purified it for him."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a man lying on his back. He said: "O servant of Allah, come near to me, take my hand and set me up, for by Allah I have not sat since Allah created me." So he took his hand, and he rose running until I could no longer see him. Then the young man said to him: "This is the life-span of the worldly one, which has run out. I am the Angel of Death, and I am the woman who came to you... Allah commanded me to seize the soul of the worldly one in this place, then I would take him to the Fire of Hell." He said: So concerning him this was revealed: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾, the verse.

This is a strange report, and its authenticity is open to question. Applying the verse to him and regarding him, in the sense that all the disbelievers are taken in death while their souls are attached to the life of this world, is as happened to this deluded and beguiled man, who went seeking his aim, and death came upon him suddenly, unexpectedly, and a barrier was placed between him and what he desired.

* *

His saying: ﴿As was done with their like before﴾, meaning, as happened to the past nations that denied the Messengers. When the punishment of Allah came upon them, they wished that they had believed, but it was not accepted from them: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. [This is] the way of Allah which has preceded among His servants. And the disbelievers were lost there.﴾ [Ghafir: 84–85].

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾, meaning, in the world they were in doubt and suspicion, and therefore faith was not accepted from them when they witnessed the punishment.

Qatadah said: "Beware of doubt and suspicion, for whoever dies upon doubt will be raised upon it, and whoever dies upon certainty will be raised upon it."

End of the commentary on Surah "Saba'". And to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they had already disbelieved in it before﴾, meaning, how can faith be attained for them in the Hereafter when they disbelieved in the truth in the world and denied the Messengers?

The correct position is that there is no contradiction between the two views, for a barrier has indeed been placed between them and their desires in the world, and between them and what they sought in the Hereafter, so they were prevented from it.

He said: There was a man from the Children of Israel who was prosperous — that is, Allah had opened wealth to him — and he died, and his worthless son inherited him — that is, corrupt — and he would spend the wealth of Allah on the disobedience of Allah. When the brothers of his father saw this, they came to the young man, blamed him and reproached him, so the young man became resentful and sold his property for cash, then travelled and came to a gushing spring, and he spent his wealth there and built a palace. One day as he was sitting, a wind carried to him a woman of the most beautiful face and the sweetest fragrance — that is, a scent — and she said: "Who are you, O servant of Allah?" He said: "I am a man from the Children of Israel." She said: "Is this palace yours, and this wealth?" He said: "Yes." She said: "Do you have a wife?" He said: "No." She said: "How can life be pleasant for you without a wife?" He said: "That was the case before." She said: "Do you have a husband?" She said: "No." He said: "Would you accept that I marry you?" She said: "I am a woman who is a mile away from you. When tomorrow comes, take provisions for a day and come to me, and if you see a terror on your way, let it not frighten you." When the next day came, he took provisions for a day and set out, until he reached a palace, and he knocked on its door, and a young man of the most beautiful face and the sweetest fragrance came out to him and said: "Who are you, O servant of Allah?" He said: "I am the Israelite." He said: "What is your need?" He said: "The mistress of this palace has invited me to herself." He said: "You have told the truth." He said: "Did you see anything terrifying on your way?" He said: "Yes, and had she not told me that there was no harm upon me, what I saw would have terrified me. I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a bitch with its mouth open. I was startled and leapt, and behold, I was behind her, and her puppies were barking in her belly." The young man said to him: "You will not understand this; this will happen at the end of time: a youth will sit with the elders in their assembly and will outdo them in speech."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a hundred ewes in full udder, and among them a kid that was sucking them; when it had reached them and thought it had left nothing, it opened its mouth seeking more. He said: "You will not understand this; this will happen at the end of time: a king will gather all the wealth of the people, and when he thinks he has left nothing, he will open his mouth seeking more."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a tree, and a branch of one of its trees pleased me because of its freshness, so I wanted to cut it, and another tree called out to me: "O servant of Allah, take from me!" Until all the trees called out together: "O servant of Allah, take from us!" He said: "You will not understand this; this will happen at the end of time: men will become few and women will become many, so that a man will propose to a woman and ten or twenty women will invite him to themselves."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a man standing over a spring, drawing water for each person; when they dispersed from him, he poured what was in his jug and nothing in his jug clung to anything of the water. He said: "You will not understand this; this will happen at the end of time: the storyteller will teach people knowledge and then will go against them into the disobedience of Allah."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a ewe, and behold, a people had taken hold of its legs, and a man had taken hold of its horns, and a man had taken hold of its tail, and a man had mounted it, and a man was milking it. He said: "As for the ewe, it is this world. Those who took hold of its legs are falling away from its life. As for the one who took hold of its horns, he struggles with distress from its life. As for the one who took hold of its tail, it has turned away from him. As for the one who mounted it, he has left it. As for the one who is milking it, well done, that has taken it away."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a man drawing from a well, and each time he brought out his bucket he poured it into a pool, and the water flowed back into the well. He said: "This is a man whom Allah has rejected his righteous deed, and He did not accept it."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a man sowing seed, which then ripens, and behold, good wheat. He said: "This is a man whose righteous deed Allah has accepted, and He has purified it for him."

He said: Then I advanced until the path opened before me, and behold, a man lying on his back. He said: "O servant of Allah, come near to me, take my hand and set me up, for by Allah I have not sat since Allah created me." So he took his hand, and he rose running until I could no longer see him. Then the young man said to him: "This is the life-span of the worldly one, which has run out. I am the Angel of Death, and I am the woman who came to you... Allah commanded me to seize the soul of the worldly one in this place, then I would take him to the Fire of Hell." He said: So concerning him this was revealed: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾, the verse.

This is a strange report, and its authenticity is open to question. Applying the verse to him and regarding him, in the sense that all the disbelievers are taken in death while their souls are attached to the life of this world, is as happened to this deluded and beguiled man, who went seeking his aim, and death came upon him suddenly, unexpectedly, and a barrier was placed between him and what he desired.

* *

His saying: ﴿As was done with their like before﴾, meaning, as happened to the past nations that denied the Messengers. When the punishment of Allah came upon them, they wished that they had believed, but it was not accepted from them: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. [This is] the way of Allah which has preceded among His servants. And the disbelievers were lost there.﴾ [Ghafir: 84–85].

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾, meaning, in the world they were in doubt and suspicion, and therefore faith was not accepted from them when they witnessed the punishment.

Qatadah said: "Beware of doubt and suspicion, for whoever dies upon doubt will be raised upon it, and whoever dies upon certainty will be raised upon it."

End of the commentary on Surah "Saba'". And to Allah belongs all praise and grace.
